The main takeaway from our work is that

a network can learn a similarity metric that can be used directly as a similarity score between two images, and can outperform a handcrafted similarity metric such as the cosine distance between two feature vectors.
the problem of learning a similarity metric for re identification can be addressed by training a deep network to output a similarity score.

by designing an architecture that is tailored to the problem of person re identification and by training on a large data set of images, we can achieve results that are comparable to the current state of the art, even though our network is much simpler and does not have as many parameters as the state of the arts.
